pr_title: session: track LastCommitTS in SessionVars and check timestamps of later txns are larger

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Issue Number: close #57165

Problem Summary:

This PR checks the invariant that timestamps of transactions in a session should increase monotonically.

It saves the timestamp of the last transaction in `SessionVars`, after the transaction is committed. The saved timestamp is compared with the `start_ts` and the `commit_ts` of the next transaction.

This PR depends on the TiKV client-go PR, https://github.com/tikv/client-go/pull/1489, which exports `commit_ts` of the transaction.

issue_context.title: server: enhance the ts check considering commit timestamp
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement
After a write transaction is committed, TiDB, as the transaction coordinator, knows the `commit_ts` used for the write transaction. This timestamp can be used as a reference to check the validity of subsequent read requests’ `read_ts`. In theory, all read requests occurring after the write transaction should use a `read_ts` greater than the previous known transaction’s `commit_ts`. 

This approach could help to expose issues like https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/56809 more quickly.


Besides, this timestamp could be considered for updating the [`tidb_low_resolution_ts`](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/system-variables#tidb_low_resolution_tso) with the known valid timestamps encountered.

review_comments: I'm not sure about this: `SnapshotTS != 0` should imply a staleness txn ctx provider? It won't hurt though
I am not sure either. That's why I named it `Preset`. The point is we don't check StartTS if it is preset.

@ekexium @b6g 

Here, considering various historical features (e.g., `tidb_snapshot`, stale read, etc.), careful attention is required to ensure accurate and comprehensive condition checks. Any oversight could lead to unexpected tidb-server panics.  

An alternative approach is to reverse the logic—confirming that the current transaction is activated by a **PD-allocated timestamp** before proceeding with the check. This seems to be a more reliable method.

like
```
- if !usePresetStartTS
+ if activiatedByPDAllocatedTS
```
How do we know a txn is activated by a PD allocated timstamp?

Perhaps we could continue by now.
/cc @you06

`usePresetStartTS` looks fine for me. But better leave a comment that we may have a flag which indicate the `start_ts` is from PD.

I took a look at the code and feel like we can add StartTSFromPD [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/43f2fb91d740aaf45774d99b71554eead12009cc/pkg/sessionctx/variable/session.go#L207), and set it to true if the `start_ts` is from a ts future [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/43f2fb91d740aaf45774d99b71554eead12009cc/pkg/session/txn.go#L295).

This field seems to overlap with the newly added `CommitTS` in the KV interface. Additionally, `LazyTxn` is a structure that is no longer needed once a transaction is completed. Or just retain only one of them?
This is because `kv.Transaction` will be set to nil in `changeToInvalid` in `LazyTxn.Commit`.

Actually the reason is `CommitTS` has to be saved until the next transaction. If we change `doCommit` to return `CommitTS`, we have to,
- save `CommitTS` in `session`
- check if the transaction is committed successfully in `doCommit`
Since we have to save to save `CommitTS`, it would be simpler to save `CommitTS` inside `doCommit`.
I think `s.txn.CommitTS` is already reset in `LazyTxn.Commit` before it reaches the defer of doCommit.
Is this comment correct? Isnt it checking the LastCommitTS is later than the StartTS instead of the other way around?
I think it is correct. It logs fatal if LastCommitTS is later than StartTS.
